newsitem.title: THAILAND: PTTEP output to rise despite lower reserve.
newsitem.headline: PTTEP output to rise despite lower reserve.

text.p: State-backed Thai energy firm PTT Exploration and Production Plc said on Monday it would proceed with plans to raise natural gas production from offshore Bongkot field despite a downward revision of its reserves.
The company, through a weekend statement, trimmed by 9.6 percent the proven gas and petroleum reserves at Bongkot in the Gulf of Thailand in which it owns a 40 percent stake.
Latest PTTEP estimates put Bongkot reserves, mostly natural gas, at 2.8 trillion cubic feet, down from 3.1 trillion estimated earlier.
"Even though the reserves are lower, it does not affect our plans to increase production to 550 (million cubic feet per day) next year," PTTEP President Prajya Phinyawat told Reuters.
The Bongkot field produced an average 350 million cubic feet per day in 1996, up from 200 million in 1994.
PTTEP vice-president of operations Maroot Mrigadet said previous reserve estimates were based on data collected in 1994.

He described Bongkot's new reserve projections as conservative, saying his company hoped to eventually develop more than its latest estimate. He said PTTEP's total proven reserves of all its fields in the gulf showed a four percent rise.
The figures do not include results from the Muda drillings in the Thai-Malaysian joint development area, or the Yetagun gas field project in Burma.
The lower Bongkot reserve estimates triggered selling of PTTEP's shares which hit a 10 percent limit low on Monday, falling 36 baht to 334, against 3.35 percent decline of the overall stock market.
PTTEP's stock recently reached to its all-time high, trading at a price/earnings ratio of over 100 times.
